A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same unlearning evaluation framework. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR10 experiments measuring unlearning quality, IC scores, and sensitivity to dataset size, random seeds, and privacy budgets.

after.justification: V2 reports original CIFAR10 experiments, including revised privacy-budget results, MIA-AUC comparisons, and a SWAP-versus-random-splits variance experiment.

M1.justification: The unlearning sample inference game, unlearning-quality metric, SWAP procedure, and weak-adversary approximation are unchanged. Clarifications to the counterexample and revised experimental settings do not introduce a proposed method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR10 image classification, including differential-privacy experiments and IC label confusion. The added comparisons retain this coverage. Sequential unlearning is discussed only as future work.

E2.justification: V2 adds an evaluated MIA-AUC comparator, reported as 1 minus AUC in Table 4, alongside the retained IC test. Table 2 additionally compares SWAP with two independent random splits. The six unlearning algorithms and selected MIA attack families remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the default unlearning fraction from 0.25 to 0.1 and DP-model training from 20 to 100 epochs, substantially revising the reported experimental settings. Figure 2 explicitly retains the 0.25 fraction. V2 also introduces the paired-versus-independent-splits control and MIA-AUC evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The dataset-size and random-seed analyses remain. V2 adds a focused split-pairing ablation in Section 4.3 and Table 2, testing whether SWAP reduces evaluation variability compared with two independently sampled splits.

E5.justification: V2 reports standard deviations across four base seeds for the new split-pairing comparison. Three-model averaging and the five-seed Figure 2 analysis already appeared in v1 and are retained; the addition does not establish increased repetitions of existing experiments.

E6.justification: The Q and IC tables contain extensively revised results: v1 Tables 2 and 1 correspond to v2 Tables 1 and 3. For example, the non-DP Q ranking of NEGGRAD and FISHER reverses, from 0.854 versus 0.795 to 0.628 versus 0.709, under revised default settings. MIA-AUC scores and SWAP/random standard deviations are newly reported. These are not established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.9 repackages v1's existing hard-coded-adversary counterexample and non-degeneracy argument. The definitions, guarantees, and appendix proofs retain their mathematical substance. Although the main-text SWAP cancellation derivation is omitted, its reasoning remains in Appendix B's pairing proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about game-based evaluation, retraining's zero adversarial advantage, certified-removal guarantees, and efficient SWAP approximation. Added experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 adds an empirical variance-stabilization rationale for SWAP and explicitly identifies the inability to evaluate successive unlearning requests in Appendix C.1. The weak-adversary caveat is retained from v1's Remark 4.1. The DP discussion is reframed around validating the certified-removal guarantee.

D1.justification: V2 newly states CIFAR10's CC-BY 4.0 license and revises the documented DP training budget and default unlearning fraction. It describes how to construct the new split-pairing comparison. Most optimizer, architecture, and averaging details were already disclosed in v1 and are reorganized.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ruder (2016) as an optimization reference and refocuses the experimental positioning on IC and MIA-AUC, including the already cited Golatkar et al. (2021). The broader related-work survey and principal novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4 is extensively rewritten and reorganized into settings, theoretical validation, empirical merits, and metric comparisons. Settings are recast around game phases, existing analyses are reordered, and the conclusion is consolidated. V2 also adds limitations and broader-impact subsections.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn at higher resolution with revised axes, legends, colors, and captions; Figure 1 adds a Defender label and adjusts its arrangement. Existing Q and IC tables are relocated and restyled, and two tables are added. The overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: The new split-pairing control directly supports SWAP's practical stability, while the MIA-AUC comparison addresses a central comparator previously only discussed. Clearer plots and the sequential-unlearning limitation also help. These gains are limited by reporting errors: Section 4.4 retains the claim that NONE beats NEGGRAD at epsilon 50, which matched v1's table but contradicts v2 Table 3's 0.749 versus 0.925. The added evidence nevertheless provides a modest net improvement.
